_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 4, against the JA. Blau notes consulted: 4:3 (בעד איאם — 'after days', no quantifier), 4:12 (תפלחהא ולא תאוד תעטיך קואהא), 4:22 (ציקל — kept as literal 'first burnisher'; Blau's emendation acknowledged as weak), 4:24 (hyperbolic 'more and more', not literal 77). Saadia's interpretive moves: ואקע = 'lay with' for ידע (intercourse); קאול = 'quarreled' for ויאמר אל הבל (Saadia infers the unstated dispute); בלד נוד = 'land of Nod' (transliterates); תבד'לת אלדעוה = Saadia takes הוחל from חלל ('was profaned') — a negative reading of the calling-on-God's-name moment.

translations.1: And Adam lay with Eve his wife; and she conceived and bore Cain. And she said: 'I have been provisioned with a man from before God.'
translations.2: Then she repeated, and bore his brother Abel; and Abel was a shepherd of sheep, and Cain was a tiller of the earth.
translations.3: And after days had passed, Cain brought from the fruit of the earth a gift to God.
translations.4: And Abel — he too — brought from the firstborn of his sheep and from their fatlings; and God accepted Abel and his gift.
translations.5: But Cain and his gift He did not accept; and it pressed greatly upon Cain, and his face fell out of shame.
translations.6: And God said to Cain: 'Why has it pressed upon you, and why has your face fallen?
translations.7: Is it not so — if you do well, you shall be accepted; but if you do not do well, then wherever you turn, your sin is crouching; and toward you is its inclination — yet you are the one set in authority over it, by free choice.'
translations.8: Then Cain quarreled with Abel his brother; and when they were in the wilderness, Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.
translations.9: And God said to him, by way of confirming: 'Where is Abel your brother?' He said: 'I do not know. Am I the keeper of my brother?'
translations.10: He said: 'What is this that you have done? The voice of the blood of your brother cries out to Me from the earth!
translations.11: And now you are cursed from the earth, which opened its mouth and received the blood of your brother from your hand.
translations.12: When you till it, it shall not again give you its strengths; a wanderer and a roamer shall you be in the earth.'
translations.13: And Cain said before God: 'My sin is greater than can be forgiven.
translations.14: If You expel me today from the face of the earth — can I be concealed from before You? And if I be a wanderer and a roamer in the earth, every one who finds me shall kill me.'
translations.15: And God said to him: 'Therefore, every one who kills Cain — vengeance shall be exacted by means of him many times over.' And God set for Cain a sign, that no one finding him should kill him.
translations.16: And Cain went out from before God, and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
translations.17: And Cain lay with his wife; and she conceived and bore Enoch; and he built a town, and named it after the name of his son, Enoch.
translations.18: Then to Enoch was born Irad; and Irad begot Mehuyael; and Mehiyael begot Methushael; and Methushael begot Lamech.
translations.19: And Lamech took for himself two wives; the name of one of them was Adah, and [the name of] the other was Tzillah.
translations.20: And Adah bore Yaval; he was the first to dwell in tents and possess cattle.
translations.22: And Tzillah, she too, bore Tuval-Cain; and he was the first burnisher of every craft of copper and iron; and his sister was Naamah.
translations.23: And Lamech said to his wives, with confidence: 'Adah and Tzillah, hear my voice; O wives of Lamech, give ear to my speech: have I killed a man by my striking, or a child by my wounding?
translations.24: If vengeance for Cain be much, then for Lamech more and more.'
translations.25: And Adam lay again with his wife; and she bore a son, and named him Seth. She said: 'God has provisioned me with another offspring, in place of Abel — since Cain killed him.'
translations.26: And to Seth, too, a son was born; and he named him Enosh. At that time, the calling upon the name of God was profaned.
